series: Licensing Before Launching Your Cosmetics Brand
approvedBy: Comparison draft — pending user approval. Not for publication.

cards.headline: Can My OEM Factory's Review Apply to My Cream?
body: Whitening and anti-wrinkle actives alone do not qualify a cream for reporting.
cards.takeaway: Check the new formula before relying on the factory's earlier review.
cards.design: Show the earlier product review notice beside the new cream formula; highlight the different product details.

cards.headline: Functional Cosmetics: Review or Report?

body.text: Functional cosmetics claim effects defined by law; if no reporting route fits, submit evidence for product review.
If the product meets Article 10 of the Enforcement Rule of the Cosmetics Act, file a review-exempt product report instead of seeking individual review.

cards.takeaway: Check whether the actual formula meets a reporting route before choosing a form.
cards.design: Use two clearly separated document columns: an individual review application versus a report based on statutory conditions.

cards.headline: Two Whitening Ingredients: Official Response
body: National Institute of Food and Drug Safety Evaluation, Mar. 9, 2026
Niacinamide 2% and alpha-bisabolol 0.5% both targeted whitening in a cream with adenosine 0.04%. The agency required individual review instead of a report.
Public petition response on the specified formula under February 2026 rules.
cards.takeaway: Even listed ingredients must form a reportable combination.
cards.design: Place the agency response summary in a document panel; show all three exact ingredient percentages, linking the two whitening ingredients.

cards.headline: When Can a Notified Product Be Reported?
body: Do functional ingredients and levels match a notified item?
Do claimed effects, directions and dosage also match?
Do the combination, criteria and test methods match?
cards.takeaway: For both whitening and wrinkle improvement, check Annex 5 of Korea's notified standards.
cards.design: Three comparison questions between a product formula and the applicable notified cosmetic item; emphasize Annex 5.

cards.headline: Can the Factory's Earlier Review Be Used?

body.text: Did the same manufacturer or responsible cosmetics distributor hold the prior review?
If the manufacturer matches, did it design, develop and produce the product?
Match ingredient type, specifications and levels; effects, test criteria, use, dose and form.

cards.takeaway: A shared OEM factory alone does not qualify the new cream for reporting.
cards.design: Zoom into the prior review holder and who actually developed the product; compare with the new formulation below.

cards.headline: Matching Rules Have Specific Exceptions

body.text: The pH standard is excluded when comparing test criteria and methods.
For specified categories, solutions, lotions and creams count as one form.
Earlier whitening or wrinkle efficacy must be shown against a control without the active ingredients.

cards.takeaway: These exceptions do not waive the other required matching conditions.
cards.design: Show pH as excluded, three allowed container forms grouped together, and efficacy proven with a control-group comparison.

cards.headline: The Final Formula Matters More Than a Promise
body: Compare it with the prior reviewed product before choosing a route.
cards.design: Give Final Formula generous typographic space; below it, display three small branching route labels.

cards.headline: Reporting and Evidence Waivers Are Different

body.text: If Article 10's reporting conditions are met, file a review-exempt report rather than seek individual review. Filing is still required.
During individual review, notified ingredients and levels, or test standards and methods, may allow some attachments to be omitted.

cards.takeaway: Does 'exempt' mean a report instead of review, or fewer attachments?
cards.design: Contrast one report form against an individual-review folder with certain attachments removed; do not depict both routes as identical.

cards.headline: Four Factory Records to Request Before Launch
body: Final formula: functional ingredients, amounts and claimed effects.
Prior review notice or reporting record, if one exists.
OEM contract: named manufacturer and supporting-document duties.
Retail name and packaging draft to compare with filing records.
cards.takeaway: After a change, check ingredient-list reporting and functional review or reporting separately.
cards.design: Arrange four distinct document sheets as a saveable checklist; use fine comparison lines between corresponding identifiers.

cards.headline: Which Filing Does Your Cream Need?

body.text: Send final functional-ingredient levels, any prior review or report, the OEM contract, product name and packaging draft.
Ethos Administrative Attorney Office's free preliminary review covers possible reporting routes, record gaps and needed factory files; drafting and permitted filings are paid.

cards.takeaway: Request a free preliminary review using your records.
cards.design: Two balanced panels: the records the reader already holds and the specific questions Ethos can review; keep paid drafting clearly separate.
